claims.statement: Krishna (कृष्ण), also Govinda, Madhava, Gopala and other names, is a major Hindu deity worshipped as the eighth avatar of Vishnu and as Supreme God in his own right, revered for love, compassion, protection and tenderness.
claims.statement_id: Kresna (कृष्ण), juga Govinda, Madhava, Gopala, dan nama lain, adalah dewa utama agama Hindu yang dipuja sebagai awatara kedelapan Wisnu dan sebagai Tuhan Yang Mahatinggi, dihormati karena kasih, welas asih, perlindungan, dan kelembutannya.
claims.quote: also known as Govinda, Madhava, Gopala, and other names and titles is a major deity in Hinduism. He is worshipped as the eighth avatar of Vishnu and as the Supreme God in his own right. He is widely revered for his divine qualities of love, compassion, protection, and tenderness.

claims.statement: Krishna's birthday is celebrated by Hindus every year on Krishna Janmashtami, in late August or early September.
claims.statement_id: Hari kelahiran Kresna dirayakan umat Hindu setiap tahun pada Krishna Janmashtami, akhir Agustus atau awal September.
claims.quote: Krishna's birthday is celebrated every year by Hindus on Krishna Janmashtami, according to the lunisolar Hindu calendar, which falls in late August or early September of the Gregorian calendar.

claims.statement: Krishna is often depicted in dark skin in accordance with the meaning of his name, 'black' or 'dark'.
claims.statement_id: Krishna sering digambarkan berkulit gelap sesuai arti namanya, 'hitam' atau 'gelap'.
claims.quote: Krishna is often depicted in dark skin in accordance with meaning of his name, "black" or "dark".

claims.statement: Krishna was born in Mathura to Devaki and Vasudeva but raised by Nanda and Yashoda in Gokul to escape his uncle, the tyrant king Kamsa.
claims.statement_id: Kresna lahir di Mathura dari Dewaki dan Wasudewa, tetapi dibesarkan Nanda dan Yashoda di Gokul untuk menghindari pamannya, raja zalim Kamsa.
claims.quote: Krishna was born in Mathura to Devaki and Vasudeva, but was raised by Nanda and Yashoda in Gokul to escape his maternal uncle, the tyrant king Kamsa.

claims.statement: Krishna enchanted the gopis with his flute, lifted Govardhan Hill to protect his community from devastating rains, defeated Kamsa, founded the city of Dvaraka and played a central role in the Kurukshetra War as Arjuna's charioteer.
claims.statement_id: Krishna memikat para gopi dengan seruling ilahinya, mengangkat Bukit Govardhan untuk melindungi kaumnya dari hujan dahsyat, mengalahkan Kamsa, mendirikan kota Dvaraka, dan berperan penting dalam perang Kurukshetra sebagai kusir kereta Arjuna.
claims.quote: he enchanted the gopis with his divine flute playing, performed the celestial Rasa Lila, and lifted Govardhan Hill to protect his community from devastating rains. He later defeated Kamsa and restored order in Mathura. He went on to establish the city of Dvaraka and played a central role in the Kurukshetra War, serving as Arjuna’s charioteer

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Krishna (Krsna or Hari Krishna) is a major god of the Hindu pantheon, considered the eighth incarnation of Vishnu, and perhaps the most popular of all the heroes of Hindu mythology.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Krishna (Krsna atau Hari Krishna) adalah dewa utama jajaran dewa Hindu, dianggap inkarnasi kedelapan Wisnu, dan mungkin yang paling populer di antara para pahlawan mitologi Hindu.
claims.quote: Krishna (Krsna or Hari Krishna) is a major god of the Hindu pantheon and considered the eighth incarnation of Vishnu. He is perhaps the most popular of all the heroes of Hindu mythology.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, Krishna is a central figure in the Mahabharata, the Bhagavata Purana, the Brahma Vaivarta Purana and the Bhagavad Gita, and these texts describe him as a divine statesman, teacher, savior of dharma, charioteer and sometimes a cowherd.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, Krishna adalah tokoh sentral dalam Mahabharata, Bhagavata Purana, Brahma Vaivarta Purana, dan Bhagavad Gita, dan teks-teks itu menggambarkannya sebagai negarawan ilahi, guru, penyelamat dharma, kusir kereta, dan kadang penggembala sapi.
claims.quote: He is a central figure in the Mahabharata, the Bhagavata Purana, the Brahma Vaivarta Purana, and the Bhagavad Gita, and is mentioned in many Hindu philosophical, theological, and mythological texts. These texts describes him as a divine statesman, teacher, savior of dharma, charioteer, and sometimes a cowherd.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Krishna's adventures appear in the Mahabharata, Bhagavad Gita, Harivamsa and the Puranas, where he is described as the Supreme Being and creator of the universe.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, petualangan Krishna muncul dalam Mahabharata, Bhagavad Gita, Harivamsa, dan Purana, yang menyebutnya Yang Mahatinggi dan pencipta alam semesta.
claims.quote: Krishna's adventures appear in the Mahabharata, Bhagavad Gita, Harivamsa, and the sacred texts known as the Puranas where he is described as the Supreme Being and creator of the universe.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Vishnu pulled two hairs from his head, one white and one black; the black hair was planted into the womb of Devaki, a princess of the city of Mathura, and Krishna was born.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Wisnu mencabut dua helai rambut, putih dan hitam; rambut hitam ditanamkan ke rahim Devaki, putri kota Mathura, dan lahirlah Krishna.
claims.quote: One day Vishnu, the great Hindu god pulled two hairs from his own head, one white and one black. The black hair was planted into the womb of Devaki, a princess of the city of Mathura

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Kamsa, his mother's brother, had been warned that Devaki's eighth child would kill him and had killed seven children before Krishna was born.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Kamsa, saudara laki-laki ibu Krishna, diperingatkan bahwa anak kedelapan Devaki akan membunuhnya, sehingga ia membunuh tujuh anak sebelum Krishna lahir.
claims.quote: Unfortunately for Krishna his mother's brother, Kamsa, had been warned that Devaki's eighth child would kill him, and so Kamsa determined to murder the eighth child, a crime he had already carried out seven times before Krishna was born.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Vasudeva hid Krishna in the remote village of Vrindavana, where he was brought up as a simple cowherd who can be called Govinda.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Wasudewa menyembunyikan Krishna di desa terpencil Vrindavana, tempat ia dibesarkan sebagai penggembala sederhana yang dapat disebut Govinda.
claims.quote: Fortunately, Vasudeva took the precaution of hiding Krishna in the remote village of Vrindavana where the boy was brought up as a simple cowherd (in this guise he can be referred to as Govinda).

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Krishna spent an idyllic childhood and stirred the hearts of many gopis with his dark good looks, playful charm and mastery of music and dance.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Krishna menghabiskan masa kecil yang indah dan memikat banyak gopi dengan ketampanannya yang gelap, pesonanya yang jenaka, serta keahliannya bermusik dan menari.
claims.quote: There he spent an idyllic childhood and stirred the hearts of many gopis or herd-women with his dark good looks, playful charm, and mastery of music and dance.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Krishna's dual role is as the punisher of human deeds but also as a bringer of enlightenment.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, peran ganda Krishna adalah sebagai penghukum perbuatan manusia sekaligus pembawa pencerahan.
claims.quote: Krishna's dual role is as the punisher of human deeds but also as a bringer of enlightenment.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Krishna's foster parents at Vrindavana were Nanda and Yashoda, his sister is Subhadra, his brother Balarama, and his favourite consort the cowherd woman Radha.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, orang tua asuh Krishna di Vrindavana adalah Nanda dan Yashoda, saudarinya Subhadra, saudaranya Balarama, dan selir kesayangannya Radha, perempuan penggembala.
claims.quote: Krishna's foster parents at Vrindavana were Nanda and Yashoda, his sister is Subhadra, and his brother Balarama. Krishna's favourite consort was the cowherd woman Radha

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Queen Rukmini, an earthly form of the goddess Lakshmi, is considered Krishna's second most favoured wife after Radha, and with Rukmini Krishna had a son, Pradyumna, and a daughter, Carumati.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Ratu Rukmini, wujud duniawi dewi Lakshmi, dianggap istri kesayangan kedua Krishna setelah Radha, dan dari Rukmini Krishna memiliki putra Pradyumna serta putri Carumati.
claims.quote: Queen Rukmini, an earthly form of the goddess Lakshmi, is considered Krishna's second most favoured wife after Radha. With Rukmini, Krishna had a son, Pradyumna, and a daughter, Carumati.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Krishna killed and thrashed prominent enemies such as the ogress Putana, the giant bull danava, the giant snake Kaliya and the king of the Hayas (horses), and dealt with the tyrant Kamsa, after whose beheading he became king of Mathura.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Krishna membunuh dan menghajar musuh-musuh terkemuka seperti raksasi Putana, banteng danava raksasa, ular raksasa Kaliya, dan raja Haya (kuda), serta mengalahkan tiran Kamsa, setelah itu ia menjadi raja Mathura.
claims.quote: Notable amongst these are his various killings and thrashings of prominent enemies such as the ogress Putana, the giant bull danava, the giant snake Kaliya, and the king of the Hayas (horses). Also swiftly dealt with was the scheming tyrant Kamsa – after whose beheading Krishna established himself as king of Mathura.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, the sea-demon Pancajana, who looked like a conch shell, lost his magic shell to Krishna, who carried it thereafter and used it as a trumpet.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, iblis laut Pancajana yang menyerupai kerang kehilangan kerang saktinya kepada Krishna, yang sejak itu membawanya dan memakainya sebagai trompet.
claims.quote: the sea-demon Pancajana who looked like a conch shell and who lost his magic shell to Krishna which the hero carried thereafter and used as a trumpet.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Krishna lifted Mount Govardhana to foil a terrible deluge sent by Indra, conquered Saubha, the floating city of the Titans, got the better of the sea-god Varuna and stole the divine discus of the fire-god Agni.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Krishna mengangkat Gunung Govardhana untuk menggagalkan banjir dahsyat kiriman Indra, menaklukkan Saubha kota terapung para Titan, mengungguli dewa laut Varuna, dan mencuri cakram ilahi milik dewa api Agni.
claims.quote: Krishna also found time to lift the mountain Govardhana to foil a terrible deluge sent by Indra, to conquer Saubha, the floating city of the Titans (daityas), got the better of the sea-god Varuna, and even managed to steal the divine discus possessed by the fire-god Agni.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Krishna acted as the warrior-prince Arjuna's charioteer in the Great War at Kurukshetra between the Pandavas (whom he supported) and the Kauravas, and on the eve of the battle he recounted the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Krishna menjadi kusir kereta pangeran-pejuang Arjuna dalam Perang Besar di Kurukshetra antara Pandawa (yang ia dukung) dan Kaurawa, dan pada malam sebelum perang itu ia melantunkan Bhagavad Gita kepada Arjuna.
claims.quote: Krishna acted as the warrior-prince Arjuna's charioteer in the Great War, the Battle of Kurukshetra, between the Pandavas (whom Krishna supported) and the Kauravas. It was on the eve of this battle that Krishna recounted the sacred song of the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, in the Bhagavad Gita Krishna states that the whole universe was created by him and all things exist in him, and Arjuna calls him divine, prior to the gods, unborn and omnipresent.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, dalam Bhagavad Gita Krishna menyatakan bahwa seluruh alam semesta diciptakan olehnya dan segala sesuatu ada di dalam dirinya, dan Arjuna menyebutnya ilahi, mendahului para dewa, tak dilahirkan, dan mahahadir.
claims.quote: It is in the Bhagavad Gita that Krishna also states that 'All this universe has been created by me; all things exist in me'. Arjuna, in the same work, tells us that Krishna is 'divine, prior to the gods, unborn, omnipresent'.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Krishna built the fortress city of Dvaraka in Gujarat, known as the 'City of Gates'; seven days after he was accidentally killed by a hunter's arrow striking his heel, Dvaraka was submerged beneath the ocean.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Krishna membangun kota benteng Dvaraka di Gujarat, dijuluki Kota Gerbang; tujuh hari setelah ia tewas secara tak sengaja oleh panah pemburu yang mengenai tumitnya, Dvaraka tenggelam di bawah laut.
claims.quote: In other adventures Krishna built the great fortress city of Dvaraka in Gujarat, known as the 'City of Gates'. Seven days after Krishna was accidentally killed by a hunter's arrow striking his heel, Dvaraka was submerged beneath the ocean.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Krishna stole the sacred Parijata tree from Indra, defeating the god, and planted it at Dvaraka, but on his death it was returned to Indra.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Krishna mencuri pohon suci Parijata dari Indra dan mengalahkannya, menanamnya di Dvaraka, tetapi setelah ia wafat pohon itu dikembalikan kepada Indra.
claims.quote: Krishna had also stolen the sacred Parijata tree from Indra, defeating the god in the process. Krishna planted the tree at Dvaraka, but upon his death it was returned to Indra.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, the worship of Krishna may have started as early as the 5th century BCE; today many believers worship him as the supreme Hindu god and he is especially revered in Bengal and Udupi in southern India.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, pemujaan Krishna mungkin bermula sedini abad ke-5 SM; kini ia dipuja banyak orang sebagai dewa Hindu tertinggi dan terutama dihormati di Bengal dan Udupi di India selatan.
claims.quote: The worship of Krishna may have started as early as the 5th century BCE. Today he is worshipped as the supreme Hindu god by many believers, and he is especially revered in Bengal and Udupi in southern India.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, Krishna is typically portrayed in Hindu art with dark skin (usually blue-black), may carry the discus Vajranabha and the club Kaumodaki given by Agni, wears a yellow robe, has a peacock feather in his hair and commonly plays a flute.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, dalam seni Hindu Krishna biasanya digambarkan berkulit gelap (biasanya biru-hitam), dapat membawa cakram Vajranabha dan gada Kaumodaki pemberian Agni, berjubah kuning, berbulu merak di rambutnya, dan umumnya memainkan seruling.
claims.quote: Krishna is typically portrayed in Hindu art with a dark skin (usually blue-black), and he may carry the cakra discus Vajranabha and the club Kaumodaki – both given to him by Agni. He typically wears a yellow robe, has a peacock feather in his long black hair, and commonly plays a flute.

claims.statement: According to the World History Encyclopedia, in Khmer art the most popular scene of Krishna's adventures is the lifting of Mt. Govardhana, frequently represented in architectural sculpture at famous sites such as Angkor Wat.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, dalam seni Khmer adegan petualangan Krishna yang paling populer adalah pengangkatan Gunung Govardhana, yang sering terpahat pada arsitektur di situs terkenal seperti Angkor Wat.
claims.quote: In Khmer art the most popular scene of Krishna's adventures is the lifting of Mt. Govardhana, and the god is frequently represented in the architectural sculpture at such famous sites as Angkor Wat.

claims.statement: In the preface to Edwin Arnold's translation, the plot of the Bhagavad Gita is a dialogue between Prince Arjuna and Krishna, the Supreme Deity, wearing the disguise of a charioteer.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pengantar terjemahan Edwin Arnold, alur Bhagavad Gita berupa dialog Pangeran Arjuna dengan Krishna, Dewa Tertinggi yang menyamar sebagai kusir kereta.
claims.quote: Its simple plot consists of a dialogue held by Prince Arjuna, the brother of King Yudhisthira, with Krishna, the Supreme Deity, wearing the disguise of a charioteer.

claims.statement: In the Bhagavad Gita (Arnold translation), Krishna says he is the Spirit seated deep in every creature's heart; from him they come, by him they live, and at his word they depart.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Bhagavad Gita (terjemahan Arnold), Krishna berkata bahwa ia adalah Roh yang bersemayam dalam hati setiap makhluk; dari-Nya mereka datang, oleh-Nya mereka hidup, dan atas titah-Nya mereka pergi.
claims.quote: I am the Spirit seated deep in every creature's heart; From Me they come; by Me they live; at My word they depart!

claims.statement: In the Bhagavad Gita (Arnold translation), Krishna says that among the Adityas he is Vishnu and among the Rudras he is Sankara.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Bhagavad Gita (terjemahan Arnold), Krishna berkata bahwa di antara para Aditya ia adalah Wisnu dan di antara para Rudra ia adalah Sankara.
claims.quote: Vishnu of the Adityas I am, those Lords of Light ... of Rudras Sankara

claims.statement: In the Bhagavad Gita (Arnold translation), Krishna shows Arjuna all his semblances, infinite, rich and divine, with changeful hues and countless forms.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Bhagavad Gita (terjemahan Arnold), Krishna memperlihatkan kepada Arjuna semua rupa-Nya yang tak terhingga, kaya, dan ilahi, dengan warna-warna yang berubah dan wujud yang tak terhitung.
claims.quote: I show thee all my semblances, infinite, rich, divine, My changeful hues, my countless forms.

claims.statement: In the Bhagavad Gita (Arnold translation), after showing his awesome form, Krishna tells Arjuna that he is once more the Krishna of the form he knew of old.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Bhagavad Gita (terjemahan Arnold), setelah menampakkan wujud-Nya yang menakjubkan, Krishna berkata kepada Arjuna bahwa ia kembali menjadi Krishna dengan rupa yang dikenalnya dahulu.
claims.quote: Once more I am thy Krishna, the form thou knew'st of old!

claims.statement: In the Vishnu Purana, Krishna upheld Mount Govardhana with one hand as if in sport, and for seven days and nights the clouds sent by Indra poured showers on the Gokula of Nanda, but its dwellers were protected by the height of the mountain.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Wisnu Purana, Krishna mengangkat Gunung Govardhana dengan satu tangan seolah bermain, dan selama tujuh hari tujuh malam awan kiriman Indra menurunkan hujan atas Gokula milik Nanda tetapi para penghuninya terlindung oleh ketinggian gunung itu.
claims.quote: Having thus made up his mind, Krishna immediately upheld the mountain Govardhana with one hand as if in sport ... For seven days and nights did the vast clouds, despatched by Indra, pour down showers upon the Gokula of Nanda, to destroy the dwellers, but they were protected by the height of the mountain.

claims.statement: In the Vishnu Purana, Krishna sees the pool with the dreadful serpent Kāliya boiling with the fires of poison and resolves to slay it so that the inhabitants of Vraja may live happily freed from fear.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Wisnu Purana, Krishna melihat kolam berisi ular dahsyat Kāliya yang mendidih oleh api bisa, dan berniat membunuhnya agar penduduk Vraja hidup bahagia tanpa rasa takut.
claims.quote: There he saw the pool with the dreadful serpent Kāliya, boiling with the fires of poison ... I must slay this serpent, so that the inhabitants of Vraja may live here happily freed from fear.

claims.statement: In the Vishnu Purana, Krishna seizes Kansa by the hair, strikes his tiara to the ground and throws him down and falls upon him, so that Kansa, the son of Ugrasena, gives up the ghost, crushed by the weight of the upholder of the universe.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Wisnu Purana, Krishna menarik rambut Kansa, menjatuhkan mahkotanya, lalu menjatuhkan Kansa ke tanah dan menimpanya, sehingga Kansa, putra Ugrasena, tewas tertindih beban sang penopang alam semesta.
claims.quote: laid hold of him by the hair of his head, and struck his tiara to the ground: then casting him down upon the earth, Govinda threw himself upon him. Crushed by the weight of the upholder of the universe, the son of Ugrasena, Kansa the king, gave up the ghost.

claims.statement: In the Vishnu Purana, a voice from the sky tells Kansa that the eighth child of Devaki shall destroy his life.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Wisnu Purana, sebuah suara dari langit berkata kepada Kansa bahwa anak kedelapan Devaki akan mengakhiri hidupnya.
claims.quote: A voice was heard in the sky, loud and deep as thunder, which addressing Kansa, said—"O foolish, the eighth child of this damsel, whom thou art carrying in the car, along with her husband, shall destroy thy life".

claims.statement: In the Vishnu Purana, the supreme deity plucks off two hairs, one white and one black, and declares that his black hair shall be impersonated in the eighth conception of Devaki, the wife of Vasudeva, and shall destroy Kansa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Wisnu Purana, Sang Dewa Tertinggi mencabut dua helai rambut, putih dan hitam, dan menyatakan bahwa rambut hitamnya akan menjelma dalam kandungan kedelapan Devaki, istri Wasudewa, dan akan membinasakan Kansa.
claims.quote: the supreme deity plucked off two hairs, one white and one black and said to the celestials ... This, my black hair, shall be impersonated in the eighth conception of the goddess-like Devaki, the wife of Vasudeva and shall destroy Kansa
